comparison: Both evaluate membrane rigidity findings (C7, C32, C33) as supported. OpenEval emphasizes FRAP experimental design and controls, while peer reviewers highlight this as a key strength with 'compelling evidence.'

Both support PUFA rescue experiments (C8, C34, C37, C39). OpenEval details dose-dependent effects and DHA rescue, while peer reviewers note rescue was 'only achieved with polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation.'

Both strongly support the critical finding that NP-40 improves fluidity but not growth (C43-C48, C60). OpenEval emphasizes this distinguishes fat-2 from paqr-2, peer reviewers accept this as evidence PUFAs have non-fluidity functions.

Both support the genetic screen design and saturation (C10, C61-C63, C124). OpenEval notes ~40,000 genomes screened, peer reviewers describe it as 'very thorough' and 'high quality' with 'near-saturation.'
Perfect agreement on fat-2 intragenic suppressors (C65-C67). Both accept the structural compensation interpretation at S99 position without challenge.

Both support egl-9 R557 mutations and separation-of-function interpretation (C68-C72, C145-C146). OpenEval details molecular mechanism, peer reviewers accept constitutive HIF-1 activation and sufficient mechanistic insights.
Both support hif-1 gain-of-function characterization (C73-C76). OpenEval emphasizes dominance testing and CRISPR validation, peer reviewers highlight value of discovering gain-of-function mutations.

Both support ftn-2 mechanism linking to Fe2+ and desaturase activation (C78-C84, C85-C88). OpenEval cites recent literature support, peer reviewers accept that 'increased iron makes FAT-2 more active.'

Both support epistasis analysis showing pathway convergence (C85-C92, C89-C92, C101, C128). OpenEval emphasizes genetic logic, peer reviewers accept that HIF-1 pathway leads to decreased ftn-2 expression.

Both support lipidomic characterization (C49-C52). OpenEval emphasizes finding that 25°C rescue occurs without PUFA changes, peer reviewers note minor limitation about 18:1 isomers but accept conclusions.

Both support lipidomic validation showing selective EPA increase (C105-C106, C135). OpenEval details statistical analysis, peer reviewers accept that suppressors increase 'desaturation and PUFA synthesis.'

Both support stress response characterization and rescue (C107-C115). OpenEval details FRAP and reporter experiments, peer reviewers accept this as part of thorough validation showing suppressors rescue multiple phenotypes.

Perfect agreement on pharmacological intervention experiments (C116-C123). Both accept largely negative results as important controls demonstrating genetic suppressors achieve effects difficult to replicate pharmacologically.

Strong agreement on main conclusion that PUFAs cannot be genetically replaced (C14-C15, C125-C127, C149-C150). Both emphasize all suppressors restore PUFA levels, demonstrating essential pleiotropic functions. Editor highlights this as key finding.

Both support HIF-1 downregulation findings and feedback regulation (C93-C100). OpenEval notes Western blot and qPCR data, peer reviewers accept as part of 'sufficient mechanistic insights' and extensive validation.
Perfect agreement on FAT-2 protein level findings (C102-C103). Both accept that S101F reduces protein levels and that suppressors don't primarily act by increasing FAT-2 abundance.
Both support adaptive response hypothesis and Fe2+ mechanism (C128-C134). OpenEval presents as novel interpretation, peer reviewers accept mechanistic logic without challenge.

Both support EPA-focused conclusions (C137-C144, C151). OpenEval integrates prior knowledge about EPA functions, peer reviewers accept EPA-centric interpretation as providing 'fundamental insights about membrane lipid composition.'

Both support negative results with paqr-2 suppressors (C57-C59, C60). OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates distinct mechanisms, peer reviewers accept this strengthens conclusion that membrane rigidity is not primary issue.
Both support EGL-9 separation-of-function interpretation (C145-C147). OpenEval cites prior work, peer reviewers accept mechanistic insights about EGL-9 function beyond HIF-1 regulation.

Both support qPCR validation of ftn-2 repression (C100-C101). OpenEval emphasizes statistical analysis, peer reviewers accept as part of molecular validation showing 'sufficient mechanistic insights.'

OpenEval evaluates background/introduction claims (C1-C6, C16-C30) as well-supported by citations. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background knowledge, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.
